diagnostic_evidence.quote: and resulted in their formal description as the star spaces of all nontrivial 2-connected series-parallel graphs on $k + 1$ vertices and $n$ edges equipped with certain positive weights and arbitrary directions.
then the column space of $W^{\frac{1}{2}} B^T$ deviates from all the coordinate $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathds{R}^n$ by at least $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$.

Having carried out our experiments for all $1 \leq k < n \leq 9$, we decided to search for the resulting triangle of numbers (see Table \ref{tab}) in the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences \cite{OEIS}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose announces a description of the whole class of subspaces whose least deviation from the coordinate subspaces is at least arccos(1/sqrt(n)) (i.e. of all extremal subspaces). The formal content only proves one inclusion: every star space of a 2-sp-graph with G-induced weights has that property (Theorem). No result shows that every subspace with the property is of this form; the only support for completeness is the matching of experimental counts for n <= 9 with OEIS A115594.

failure_location.quote: we describe the class of subspaces deviating from all the coordinate ones by at least $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Narrow the abstract and introduction to a construction claim ("we construct/describe a class of subspaces deviating by at least arccos(1/sqrt(n))") and restate completeness as a conjecture supported by the reported experiments; no formal result needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: The classification/completeness claim made in the abstract and introduction is unsupported; only the sufficiency direction (a construction of subspaces with deviation at least arccos(1/sqrt(n))) is established.
issues.title: Abstract and introduction claim a complete classification that is never proved
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the prose preserves the construction, the theorem and the corollary, but the promised classification is a substantive claim that must be withdrawn (or supplied with a new classification argument), so the repair exceeds a minor local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We leave it as an exercise for the reader to prove the following property.
Graph-tree-induced edge coefficients are invariant to the choice of terminals up to a common factor.
where $y_\tau$ is the restriction of the vector of $(G,\tau)$-induced coefficients to the set of $\tau$'s edges

issues.failure_explanation: The (G,tau)-induced coefficients y_e are defined through a decomposition chain that depends on the chosen terminal pair. In the proof, each coordinate e_0 of the claimed identity (T Y_tau y_tau)(e_0) = (T/n) y_tau(e_0) is treated after re-choosing the terminals to be the endpoints of that very edge e_0, so a different coefficient vector is used for each coordinate. Concluding Y_tau y_tau = (1/n) y_tau for one fixed nonzero vector requires exactly the content of Proposition prop:added-1 (all these vectors are proportional), and that proposition is stated with no proof at all.

failure_location.quote: Let us denote $e_0$'s vertices by $l$ and $r$ and treat them as the terminals.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove Proposition prop:added-1 (terminal-invariance of the (G,tau)-induced coefficients up to a common factor), along the lines of the already-given proof of Proposition prw, and invoke it to identify the per-e_0 coefficient vectors up to scale.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:added-1 is incomplete: as written it produces, for each edge of tau, a vanishing single coordinate of (Y_tau - (1/n)I)y, which does not yield an eigenvector. Consequently Theorem thm:added-1 and, through it, Corollary cor:added-1 are left unestablished.
issues.title: Main theorem's eigenvector argument silently needs the unproved terminal-invariance proposition
issues.why_classification: The missing input is a self-contained, genuinely nontrivial lemma (an analogue of Proposition prw) plus its invocation; supplying it keeps the statement, the construction and the corollary intact, so no new global architecture or loss of content is needed, yet the repair is more than a routine local edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all the experiments we have conducted for various $n$ and $k$, this value was equal to $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$.

issues.failure_explanation: d is the target function, i.e. the least deviation measured as the largest principal angle, and the paper states its extremal value is arccos(1/sqrt(n)). The algorithm nevertheless compares d with 1/sqrt(n) +/- epsilon. Since arccos(1/sqrt(n)) > 1/sqrt(n) for every n >= 2 (e.g. 0.785 vs 0.707 for n = 2, 0.955 vs 0.577 for n = 3), the branch that prints "The hypothesis is solved in negative" and aborts triggers precisely on the extremal subspaces the algorithm is designed to collect (for any epsilon < arccos(1/sqrt(n)) - 1/sqrt(n)), while the acceptance test d > 1/sqrt(n) - epsilon also admits subspaces that are not extremal.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both thresholds 1/sqrt(n) by arccos(1/sqrt(n)) (equivalently, redefine Distance to return the corresponding cosine and reverse the optimization and comparison directions); the heuristic method and its advertised output then survive.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:cap2 fails its stated contract: it cannot return a set of extremal subspaces ES and issues a false negative-solution report; the counts in Table tab could not be produced by it as written.
issues.title: Extremal-subspace algorithm thresholds 1/sqrt(n) instead of arccos(1/sqrt(n))
issues.why_classification: A short local correction of the two thresholds (or of the returned quantity together with the comparison directions) restores the algorithm's guarantee without any new lemma, construction or reoptimization.
